statement: There are n courses, numbered 0 to n − 1. You are given graph, made of the vertex count n and a list of edges [a, b], each meaning course a must be finished before course b can be taken.

Return an order in which all n courses can be taken while respecting every prerequisite. If several orders work, any of them is accepted; the one shown here is produced by Kahn's algorithm, which starts from courses with no prerequisites in increasing order.
If no such order exists, because the prerequisites form a cycle, return an empty list.

examples.explanation: Course 0 has no prerequisites. Taking it unlocks 1 and 2, and taking both of those unlocks 3. The order [0, 2, 1, 3] would also be valid.
Courses 0 and 1 each require the other, so neither can ever be taken. Course 2 is free, but a full schedule is impossible, so the answer is an empty list.
